summary: Android shows an inset, fully visible rounded dialog over a dark scrim, while React shows a near-full-width sheet with only its top corners visible and lower content cropped by the viewport.

The header differs: React places the close icon left of the title, adds a divider, and shows a disabled Create button at top right; Android moves close to the top right, omits the divider and header button, and adds a Cancel/Create footer.

The rendered forms differ substantially. React shows custom-provider URL, Authentication/API key, Model, Reasoning, Fast mode, and Advanced fields; Android shows an agent-limit banner, Computer choices, Name, Description, and Runtime fields.
Android's Create Agent title and form labels are visibly heavier, and its input borders are thicker with larger text; React uses lighter typography and thinner outlined controls.
Android introduces state-specific visuals absent on React: a peach bordered limit warning, selected and disabled radio buttons, a peach runtime warning, and a disabled Create button.
likelyCauses: Android is rendering the general Create Agent form rather than the Claude custom-provider branch rendered by React.
The platforms use different modal containers: Android uses a centered dialog with a footer action bar, while React uses a lower, sheet-style container.
Android is applying different component-level typography, border, padding, and disabled-state tokens.
The Android custom-provider branch is omitting the header Create action, divider, refresh icons, and custom-provider fields.
analysis.suggestedOwner: Android Create Agent dialog team, with shared design-system support
suggestedFixes: Route this Android state to the Claude custom-provider form and render the URL, Authentication/API key, Model, Reasoning, Fast mode, Advanced, and Claude Command controls.
Match the React sheet bounds, top offset, visible corner radii, dark scrim, and bottom overflow/cropping behavior.
Move the close icon to the left of the title, restore the header divider and disabled Create button, and add refresh icons beside Authentication and Model.
Align title, label, input, helper-text, border-width, padding, disabled, and warning colors with the React design tokens.
If the Android content is intentional, capture the baseline against the same form state and interaction data rather than comparing different dialog variants.

summary: Component bounds differ: React fills the 390×844 viewport edge-to-edge, while Android uses a smaller centered rounded modal over a dark gray scrim.
Headers differ: React shows “Settings” plus the “Channel #design” subtitle; Android shows only “Edit Channel” and omits the subtitle.
Pin controls differ: React has a “Preferences” heading, helper copy, and an off-state switch; Android omits these and shows a full-width outlined “Pin” action button.

Cancel and Save differ in placement and state: Android places them below the fields with a disabled gray Save, while React places them at the bottom right with an active pink Save.
likelyCauses: The Android implementation uses a dialog component rather than React's full-screen panel component.
The Android feature specification omits or restructures the Preferences and Channel actions sections.

Match React's field heights, border weight, corner radius, and focused Name-field outline, especially the taller Description textarea.

cases.title: Members Create Agent Dialog - no computer branch

summary: React displays a compact modal containing a blue "Connect a computer first" notice, while Android displays a near-full-height create-agent form.
Android omits the blue explanatory panel and pink "Add Computer" button; it instead shows an orange agent-limit banner and a disabled gray "Create" button.
Android adds Computer, Name, Description, runtime-selection controls, and a character counter that are absent from React.
The modal bounds differ substantially: React uses a short, wide card around 365×245 px, whereas Android spans roughly 350×775 px with narrow side margins.
Typography, internal padding, and vertical spacing scale with the full-height Android form instead of matching the compact React layout.
likelyCauses: Android is rendering the default create-agent dialog instead of the dedicated no-computer branch.
The no-computer condition is represented as an inline empty Computer field rather than replacing the create flow.
Condition precedence or test fixture state differs: Android renders an agent-limit warning that is absent on React.
suggestedFixes: When no computer is connected, render the same dedicated no-computer modal as React and suppress the full agent form.
Match React's compact card width, height, corner radius, vertical placement, and internal padding.
Replace the Android form-only content in this state with the blue notice, explanatory copy, text-style Cancel action, and pink outlined "Add Computer" button.
Align title, notice, body-text, and action typography weights and sizes with the React baseline.
Verify no-computer and agent-limit fixtures independently, then rerun the Slock comparison at 390×844.
